Quantum Genetic Algorithm

Source: R/QGA.R
QGA.Rd

Runs a Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA) to optimize a user-defined fitness function over discrete decision variables. Internally it initializes a quantum population, iterates measurement, rotation, and optional mutation and interference, repairs invalid genes, evaluates fitness (in parallel if `parallel = TRUE`), and tracks best/average fitness across generations.

QGA(
  popsize = 20,
  generation_max = 200,
  nvalues_sol,
  Genome,
  thetainit = 3.1415926535 * 0.05,
  thetaend = 3.1415926535 * 0.025,
  pop_mutation_rate_init = NULL,
  pop_mutation_rate_end = NULL,
  mutation_rate_init = NULL,
  mutation_rate_end = NULL,
  mutation_flag = TRUE,
  plotting = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  progress = TRUE,
  eval_fitness,
  eval_func_inputs,
  stop_limit = NULL,
  stop_iters = NULL,
  interference_flag = FALSE,
  interference_rate = 0.1,
  interference_type = c("diagonal", "amplitude"),
  interference_lambda = 0.5,
  epsilon = 0,
  restart_iters = NULL,
  restart_strength = 0.5,
  restart_theta = FALSE,
  attractor_type = c("generation", "personal"),
  migration_group_size = 2,
  migration_local_period = 1,
  migration_global_period = 50,
  parallel = FALSE
)

Arguments

popsize

Integer. Population size.

generation_max

Integer. Maximum number of generations to run.

nvalues_sol

Integer. Number of allowed discrete values per gene (1..nvalues_sol).

Genome

Integer. Number of genes (decision variables).

thetainit

Numeric (radians). Initial rotation step for the update rule.

thetaend

Numeric (radians). Final rotation step (linearly decayed to this value).

pop_mutation_rate_init

Numeric in [0,1]. Initial per-individual mutation probability (default `1/(popsize+1)` when `mutation_flag`).

pop_mutation_rate_end

Numeric in [0,1]. Final per-individual mutation probability (default `1/(popsize+1)` when `mutation_flag`).

mutation_rate_init

Numeric in [0,1]. Initial per-bit mutation probability (default `1/(Genome+1)` when `mutation_flag`).

mutation_rate_end

Numeric in [0,1]. Final per-bit mutation probability (default `1/(Genome+1)` when `mutation_flag`).

mutation_flag

Logical. Whether to apply the mutation operator.

plotting

Logical. If TRUE, plots fitness history over generations.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE, prints per-generation summary to console.

progress

Logical. If TRUE, shows a text progress bar.

eval_fitness

Function. User-provided function with signature `function(solution_integers, eval_func_inputs)` returning a numeric fitness value.

eval_func_inputs

Any. Second argument passed through to `eval_fitness`.

stop_limit

Numeric. Early-stop threshold; stops when best fitness >= `stop_limit`.

stop_iters

Integer or NULL. If set, stops when there is no improvement over `stop_iters` generations.

interference_flag

Logical. Whether to apply the interference operator after mutation (see `interference_type`). Default FALSE.

interference_rate

Numeric in [0,1]. Probability of applying the interference operator to the population at each iteration. Default 0.1.

interference_type

Character. Type of interference operator: `"diagonal"` (default) copies the amplitudes of each qubit from another individual following a diagonal scheme (Narayanan & Moore, 1996), without using fitness; `"amplitude"` adds to each qubit the fitness-weighted sum of the amplitudes of the whole population, so that amplitudes of individuals above the average fitness interfere constructively and those below the average destructively. See `interference()`.

interference_lambda

Numeric >= 0. Strength of the amplitude interference (used only with `interference_type = "amplitude"`). Default 0.5.

epsilon

Numeric in \[0, 0.5). H-epsilon gate (Han & Kim, 2004): the probability of each bit value is kept in \[`epsilon`, 1 - `epsilon`\], so that qubits never collapse to a deterministic state. Default 0 (no gate).

restart_iters

Integer or NULL. If set, when the best fitness does not improve for `restart_iters` generations, the population (except the best individual) is partially brought back towards equal probabilities. Should be smaller than `stop_iters`. Default NULL (no restart).

restart_strength

Numeric in \[0, 1\]. Fraction of the way each qubit angle is moved towards pi/4 at a restart (1 = full reset). Default 0.5.

restart_theta

Logical. If TRUE, at each restart the rotation angle is brought back to `thetainit` and decays again linearly to `thetaend` over the remaining generations. Default FALSE.

attractor_type

Character. What each individual is rotated towards: `"generation"` (default), the best individual of the current generation; `"personal"`, its own attractor, i.e. the best solution it has found so far, shared through local and global migration (Han & Kim, 2002).

migration_group_size

Integer. Size of the groups of consecutive individuals for local migration (`attractor_type = "personal"`). Default 2.

migration_local_period

Integer or NULL. Every this many generations, the best attractor of each group is copied to the group. Default 1.

migration_global_period

Integer or NULL. Every this many generations, the best attractor is copied to all individuals. Default 50.

parallel

Logical. If TRUE, fitness evaluation is distributed over `detectCores() - 1` workers via `foreach`/`doParallel`. Default FALSE (sequential evaluation, no cluster is created).

Value

A list with two elements: - `best_solution_integers`: Integer vector of length `Genome` with values in 1..`nvalues_sol`. - `fitness_history_df`: Data frame with columns `generation`, `fitness_average`, `fitness_best`.

Details

Solutions are encoded as bitstrings and decoded to integer values in the range 1..`nvalues_sol` for each of the `Genome` genes. The user must supply a fitness function `eval_fitness(solution_integers, eval_func_inputs)` that returns a numeric score to maximize.

See also

`rotation()`, `mutation()`, `measure()`, `repair()`

Examples

# Minimal example (toy fitness: sum of gene values)
set.seed(1)
f <- function(sol, data) sum(sol)

# This call is illustrative; tune popsize/generation_max for real problems
# out <- QGA(popsize = 10, generation_max = 5,
#            nvalues_sol = 4, Genome = 3,
#            eval_fitness = f, eval_func_inputs = NULL,
#            plotting = FALSE, verbose = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
